# Current rules

*Generated by `plan/tools/current_rules.py` from `decisions.md` and `plan/rule_groups.yaml`. Do not edit by hand:
`python3 plan/check_plan.py` fails if this file is stale (R-292).*

Every ruling in force, grouped, each under its number. The line is the ruling's heading in `decisions.md`, which
holds its full text and why it was made. A ruling amended in part says what of it is still in force and names the
rulings that amend it; read them with it. A ruling superseded outright is left out, and the ruling that supersedes
it is listed (R-293). The one-off acts, such as a split, an acceptance or a merge, come last, as history only.

Still in force: all of it; the table gains Heggie × the generalised (Störmer–Verlet) leapfrog, measured bad, with its warning (R-567). Amended by R-567 (Heggie × the generalised leapfrog, measured bad).
- **R-562** — Regularisation is v1, not v2: integrator contract Part 6's "v2" text and REQ-INT-033 are removed
- **R-563** — The integration floor follows the occupant: with regularisation off the substep machinery is unchanged; under a regularised occupant running out of the step budget makes the result undetermined, never discarded, and the separation floor and the entry-cap hits are counted, non-terminal signals; REQ-SCHED-063 and REQ-SCHED-077 are re-pointed
- **R-565** — The sync grid is a fixed quantum of physical time, `Δ_sync`, the same for every run and independent of the horizon and of frame timing: steps are sized from it, the march stops only on it, the playhead reads boundary states, so live march, catch-up and re-boot reach the same state bitwise; time windows such as the closure window are stated in physical time
- **R-566** — Under a regularised occupant the energy is named twice: the two-body collision gate (REQ-VAL-045) and any per-step suspect flag read the regularised energy; the Cartesian energy is for diagnostics, read only from runs that did not stop at an event *(refines R-257 as to the radial collision gate's energy)*
- **R-567** — The generalised (Störmer–Verlet) leapfrog's growth under Heggie is explained: it does not keep Heggie's Eq. (9), `Σ qᵢ = 0`; Heggie × the generalised leapfrog is measured bad, with its warning, and stays allowed like every other pair *(amends R-561)*
- **R-570** — Latent and flat charts have no limit on pan or zoom-out: every latent `z` decodes to a system, so a pan never stops there and R-469's stop never fires for it; zoom-out is limited only by the frame budget and the baseline cover, a frame's cost set by the screen, not by the view's extent; every pixel is a system at any pan or zoom; far out the field goes flat by the decoder's saturation, which is correct and is never clamped, rescaled, wrapped or faded; precision is never a navigation limit *(states what R-407, R-467, R-469 and RQ-409 (a) imply; carries RQ-409 (a)'s "no zoom-out limit" from periodic charts to every chart whose axes are affine)*

## Process

- **R-175** — The reviewers are agents, and a CI check counts their verdicts *(closes H3)*. Still in force: the `VERDICT` review headings, and `reviews-complete` passing only when every named role has approved on the latest commit; R-260 carries an approval over qa's own test commit, and R-261 passes a PR naming no task. Who merges is R-369's: the orchestrator merges a PR once its reviews pass and CI is green. Amended by R-260, R-261 and R-369.
- **R-176** — Controls come before the tests that need them *(closes G3, S2)*. Still in force: TASK-M0-02 and TASK-M0-03 depend on TASK-M0-04 and register controls for their xtask tests, controls reach xtask tests through a dev-dependency on `crates/validation`, and crates without the `controls` feature are skipped; the name matching is R-199's. Amended by R-199.
- **R-177** — Cadence *(closes G4, C6)*
- **R-180** — pr-check is item-level *(closes A5)*
- **R-197** — Who may fix, suppress or configure a lint *(closes RQ-134)*
- **R-199** — A test is matched to its control by name in the macro call *(amends R-176; closes RQ-136)*. Still in force: no test-name attribute and no proc-macro crate; `negative_control!` names its test, and `cargo xtask controls` pairs tests and controls by that name; R-212 adds the expected panic message. Amended by R-212.
- **R-201** — A kernel or ledger unit test's control is registered from that crate's `tests/`, by name *(closes RQ-138)*
- **R-204** — When to ask the human. Still in force: don't ask what follows from an existing ruling or the docs: apply it and record it. What to ask the human is R-369's list (physics where the choice changes results and the docs don't settle it, calibration values, passing a milestone gate, dropping or deferring a requirement, anything outside the repo or irreversible); size is never asked (R-264, R-369).
